title: Reporting Burden Analysis

report_volume.trend_detail: Early 100-series sessions averaged 2.7 files (mostly 1 MD summary). 300-series jumped to 13.2 files/session. 700-series averaged 9.9. 800-series averages 11.7. The 500-series (3.7 avg) is an outlier — mostly single-MD case-bank remediation sessions. Post-S300, the norm is 10-13 files per session.

consumed_vs_ignored.consumption_rationale: Of ~914 session-prefixed files, approximately 320 (Session Summaries + milestone Dashboards + Risk Registers + Forecasts consumed downstream) are actually referenced by later sessions. The remainder (~594 files, 65%) are one-off artifacts: agent reports, per-session dashboards, snapshot audits, duplicate dashboard variants, and meta-reporting packages.

data_duplication.estimated_total_appearances: ~450+ across all sessions (appears in ~8 files per reporting session × 60+ reporting sessions)

data_duplication.data_point: EW fill rate / EW gap metrics

recommended_consolidation: MANDATORY: Merge multiple dashboard variants per session into a single SESSIONXXX_DASHBOARD.json. S310 produced 7 dashboard files (certification, domain, EW, executive, forecast, modernization, risk, UIQS). One is sufficient.

MANDATORY: Eliminate REPORTING_PACKAGE meta-reports (S723_REPORTING_PACKAGE.json, S802_REPORTING_PACKAGE.json, S803_REPORTING_PACKAGE.json). These are reports about reporting — a recursion with zero downstream value.

HIGH: Consolidate individual agent reports into session summary. S301 produced 26 agent files (A-Z); S8091 produced 8 agent files. These should be embedded in or summarized within the session summary MD — not persisted as standalone JSON.
HIGH: Merge PORTFOLIO_IMPACT_ANALYSIS + CERTIFICATION_RESULTS + QUALITY_GATE_RESULTS into a single 'Session Results Package' per session. Currently 3 separate files with heavily overlapping data.
MEDIUM: Merge FORECAST + COMPLETION_FORECAST into a single file. Many sessions produce both.
MEDIUM: Archive all 100-series incremental status logs to a single consolidated history file. S100-S135 sessions (62 sessions, 170 files) have zero downstream consumption.
MEDIUM: Eliminate duplicate certified-count storage. Establish a single SESSION_STATUS file as the authoritative certified count — all other files reference it rather than storing their own copy.

LOW: Standardize subdirectory organization. Currently sessions scatter outputs across reports/ root, session_status/, systematic_testing/, sessions/, S809.2/, S810.1/, and session806/. Consistent per-session output directories would improve traceability.
LOW: Deprecate non-standard naming conventions. S809.2_AGENT_*, s116_pilot_*, S722A_*, etc. Adopt SESSIONXXX_ prefix consistently.
GOVERNANCE: Add a 'max 8 files per session' soft cap to AGENTS.md. Sessions exceeding 8 files must include a BLOCK-AUTHORIZED marker (same governance pattern as the 30-item batched-write cap).
summary: The reports/ directory contains 1,212 files (829 JSON, 371 MD) across 178 unique sessions. Reporting volume has GROWN from 2.7 files/session (100-series) to 10-13 files/session (300/700/800-series). The single largest driver is agent-specific JSON outputs: S301 produced 26 agent files alone. Approximately 65% of reports are one-off artifacts never referenced by later sessions. The certified item count is duplicated across ~8 files per session (~450 total appearances), representing the most severe data duplication. Key categories (Dashboard, Forecast, Risk Register, Portfolio Impact, Certification Results) frequently overlap in content. Recommended: merge dashboard variants, eliminate reporting-package meta-reports, consolidate agent outputs into session summaries, and establish an 8-file soft cap per session.
